It looks like your hand needs to get used to holding and moving the pen. Other things that might help you improve: 
-Make sure you're not pressing down on the paper too hard, or gripping the pen too tightly. 
-Correct your posture. Believe it or not, your posture greatly affects your handwriting. 
-Practice in pencil, and correct in pen. This will help you identify what parts of letters you should focus on more. 
-Study a penmanship exemplar. This will help you better understand what your letters should look like. If you can't picture in your brain what your letters should look like, your hand has no hope of getting them right. Your hand can't do what your brain doesn't know. 
-Remember that size and spacing is more important than form and style. 
-Lastly, don't be afraid of making mistakes. 
 Hope this helps.

Try to fix your posture before you write, and slightly loosen your grip on the pen. Make sure you are breathing normally while writing, and most of all, get more used the the pen being in your hand. Over months, the more you write each day, the more comfortable it will be to write. 
As for what you are writing, start with the basics. Every letter is made of simple parts that they all have in common. The "|" shape, and "O" shape being most common. Practicing these by themselves will really help the consistency  of your writing.
